config.title: text-overflow and white-space

intro.title: text-overflow and white-space
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage that demonstrates how to control text that overflows its container. You will learn the core CSS concepts of text-overflow and white-space to manage text wrapping and truncation. The main technologies involved are CSS properties like white-space: nowrap, overflow: hidden, and text-overflow: ellipsis. By the end, you'll be able to create clean, user-friendly text displays that handle long content gracefully.
intro.usecase: The text-overflow and white-space properties are essential for creating clean, readable interfaces where space is limited. In data-rich dashboards, they prevent long text entries in table cells or card titles from breaking layouts. E-commerce sites use them to truncate product names in search results and navigation menus while maintaining consistent alignment. Form designers apply these properties to keep input field labels and error messages contained within their designated areas.

objectives: Apply the white-space property to control text wrapping behavior in CSS
Configure the text-overflow property to handle overflowing text content
Implement ellipsis truncation for single-line text elements
Construct CSS rules that combine white-space and text-overflow for specific text display scenarios
Manipulate text layout by adjusting white-space values like nowrap, pre, and normal
Control text overflow behavior using values such as clip and ellipsis
Initialize proper container constraints to make text-overflow effects visible

steps.title: Create a container with text content
steps.instruction: Create a div element with the class 'text-container' containing a long paragraph of text.
steps.hint: Write a div element with class='text-container' and put a paragraph inside with some long text.
steps.seedCode: /* Create a div with class 'text-container' containing a long paragraph of text */
steps.expectedOutcome: A div container with class 'text-container' is created, containing a paragraph with long text.
successCriteria: The HTML includes a div with class 'text-container' and a paragraph with long text inside.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the div with class 'text-container' and a paragraph with long text inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container structure isn't quite right. You need a div element with class='text-container' containing a paragraph with long text.

steps.title: Set basic container dimensions and border
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to set the width to 300px, height to 100px, and add a 1px solid black border to the .text-container class.
steps.hint: Use the width, height, and border properties in your CSS rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .text-container class will have defined dimensions and a visible border, creating a constrained area for text.
successCriteria: The .text-container rule includes width: 300px;, height: 100px;, and border: 1px solid black;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added all three required properties: width, height, and border.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule should include width: 300px;, height: 100px;, and border: 1px solid black; for the .text-container class.

steps.title: Introduce the white-space property
steps.instruction: Add the white-space property with value 'nowrap' to the .text-container class to prevent the text from wrapping to the next line.
steps.hint: Use the CSS property white-space: nowrap; inside the .text-container rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .text-container rule will include white-space: nowrap; to control text wrapping behavior.
successCriteria: The CSS contains white-space: nowrap; within the .text-container selector.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added 'white-space: nowrap;' exactly as specified.
steps.feedbackWrong: The white-space property with value 'nowrap' is missing or incorrect. Please add it to the .text-container class.

steps.title: Add overflow property
steps.instruction: Inside the .text-container selector, add the overflow property and set its value to 'hidden'.
steps.hint: The overflow property controls what happens when content overflows its container. Setting it to 'hidden' will hide any content that goes beyond the container's boundaries.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .text-container selector now includes an overflow property set to 'hidden', which will hide any content that overflows the container's dimensions.
successCriteria: The .text-container selector contains the property 'overflow: hidden;'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added 'overflow: hidden;' inside the .text-container selector. Check that the property name and value are spelled correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The overflow property hasn't been added correctly. Inside the .text-container selector, add 'overflow: hidden;' to hide content that overflows the container.

steps.title: Apply text-overflow: ellipsis
steps.instruction: Add the text-overflow property with value 'ellipsis' to the .text-container rule to show '...' for overflowed text.
steps.hint: The text-overflow property works with overflow: hidden and white-space: nowrap to display ellipsis when text is truncated.
steps.expectedOutcome: The text-overflow property is added to the .text-container rule with value 'ellipsis', enabling ellipsis display for truncated text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added text-overflow: ellipsis; to the .text-container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The text-overflow property with value 'ellipsis' is missing from the .text-container rule.

steps.title: Create a second container with different white-space value
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS rule for a class named 'text-container-2' and set its white-space property to 'pre'.
steps.hint: Add a new CSS selector starting with .text-container-2 and include the white-space property inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A second CSS rule for .text-container-2 is created with white-space: pre.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a .text-container-2 selector with white-space: pre property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the .text-container-2 rule, but make sure to include white-space: pre inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .text-container-2 with white-space: pre is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Apply text-overflow: clip to second container
steps.instruction: In the .text-container-2 rule, add the text-overflow property with the value 'clip'.
steps.hint: The text-overflow property controls how text behaves when it overflows. Use 'clip' to cut off the text abruptly at the container's edge.
steps.expectedOutcome: The second container will now cut off overflowing text abruptly instead of showing an ellipsis.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added text-overflow: clip to the .text-container-2 rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second container doesn't have text-overflow: clip applied. Add the property with the correct value to the .text-container-2 rule.

steps.title: Create a third container with word-wrap
steps.instruction: Create a third CSS class named '.text-container-3' with the same width, height, and border as the previous containers, and add 'word-wrap: break-word' to handle long unbreakable words.
steps.hint: Copy the basic container styles from '.text-container' and add the word-wrap property to allow long words to break and wrap to the next line.
steps.expectedOutcome: A third CSS class will be created with the same dimensions and border as the previous containers, plus the word-wrap property to handle long words.
successCriteria: The '.text-container-3' class exists with width: 300px, height: 100px, border: 2px solid #ccc, and word-wrap: break-word.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the container, but it's missing some required properties. Make sure it has the same width, height, and border as the other containers, plus word-wrap: break-word.
steps.feedbackWrong: The third container wasn't created correctly. Please create a '.text-container-3' class with the specified properties.

steps.title: Combine white-space and text-overflow with hover effect
steps.instruction: Add a hover effect to the first container that changes white-space to 'normal' to reveal the full text.
steps.hint: Use the :hover pseudo-class on .text-container to override the white-space property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The first container will show the full text when hovered over, demonstrating interactive overflow behavior.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the hover rule specifically targets .text-container and sets white-space to 'normal'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hover effect is missing or incorrect. Add a :hover rule for .text-container with white-space: normal.

steps.title: Review and compare all three containers
steps.instruction: Add a descriptive label before each container to explain which text-overflow technique it demonstrates.
steps.hint: Add a paragraph element with a class like 'label' before each .text-container class, then style it with basic typography.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three labeled containers showing different text-overflow behaviors (ellipsis, clip, and word-wrap) for easy comparison.
successCriteria: Each container has a descriptive label explaining its text-overflow technique, and all containers are arranged vertically.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some labels, but make sure each container has a descriptive label and they're properly styled for readability.
steps.feedbackWrong: The containers aren't labeled yet. Add descriptive text before each container to explain which text-overflow technique it demonstrates.
